page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Stop codon defined
steps.margin_note: Definition, the no-amino-acid point, and the alternative names.
lines: A STOP CODON is a codon that TERMINATES protein
Stop codons do NOT code for any amino acid.
They are also called nonsense or termination
steps.why: A stop codon has no matching tRNA, so the ribosome finds nothing to add and the chain is released.
common_mistakes: Saying stop codons code for an amino acid. They code for NONE.
Saying there is one stop codon. There are THREE.
steps.memory_tip: Nothing matches them, so the chain ends.

steps.label: The three codons
steps.margin_note: All three triplets and the 61-and-3 arithmetic.
lines: Of the 64 codons, 61 code for amino acids and
steps.why: Sixty-one coding codons plus three stop codons makes sixty-four, which is the arithmetic check that the list is complete.
common_mistakes: Writing AUG among them. AUG is the START codon.
Giving two codons. There are three.
